title: This Kid Sells a CRAZY Amount of Burgers ($1.4M/Year)...How?!

speakers.name: Henry
speakers.role: guest, 22-year-old founder of Smashers burger restaurant, Norfolk VA

idea.name: Smash burger food trailer scaled to a brick-and-mortar restaurant
idea.one_liner: Perfect one simple smash burger/fresh-cut fries/shakes menu via YouTube, test it from a $40K Craigslist food trailer on an untapped beachfront, then open a second-generation burger restaurant unit and grow with daily humorous short-form video
idea.customer: local diners and beachgoers in Norfolk/Virginia Beach
idea.offer: smash burgers, beef-tallow fries and milkshakes
idea.revenue_model: restaurant and trailer food sales (75% in-store, 25% online/delivery)

key_quotes.quote: When looking for your first restaurant, you wanna make sure that's a second generation restaurant, the previous tenant to this was Fat Burger, and that was a burger concept.
I like the food truck just because you can really test your concept before you make a massive decision like signing a lease on a brick and mortar spot.
And I didn't know what to expect from it, but like literally that weekend, we got 200 new customers from that video.

claims.quote: - This 22 year old makes $120,000 a month selling burgers.
- Yeah, we did about 90, 100 grand each summer, and it was about two and a half months each, you know.

claims.claim: Restaurant all-in cost ~$550K incl. TIA; rent ~$7K/month
claims.quote: And then after about four summers of running it, then started the restaurant and all in it came out to about 550 grand.
It's typically in the range of nine grand to 11 grand, depending on the season, every single week.

claims.claim: Commissary kitchen + second food truck was biggest waste (~$50-60K build-out)
claims.quote: It's my biggest waste of money yet.

acquisition_channels.details: daily anti-corporate humorous reels on four platforms (fake robbery skit went viral); videographer paid instead of ads
occasional Meta ads boosting best food video locally
online ordering via own app/site and DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub

ideas.delivery: simple menu; checklists/policies for staff; Restaurant Depot early then PFG distributor; certified Angus beef; prime cost target ~56%
ideas.other_uk_rules: Food business registration and hygiene rating; street trading licence for trailers; premises licence if late-night refreshment after 11pm
